onboarding.title: Welcome to Mobile Networked Creativity
onboarding.intro: Mobile Networked Creativity (MNC) maps real-world examples of how communities around the world creatively adapt mobile and networked technology to meet local needs.
onboarding.point1: Explore case studies across the globe, by location and by theme
onboarding.point2: Click any pin to read how a community adapted technology to its needs
onboarding.point3: Add your own photos and comments to contribute related examples
onboarding.footer: Mobile Networked Creativity is a project of the Scalable Design Participation Lab at Northeastern University

admin.title: Account management
admin.subtitle: Register, then an administrator grants moderation access — no Firebase console needed.
admin.registerHint: Create a plain account with your email — it carries no rights by itself. An administrator will then grant you moderation access here.
admin.errProviderDisabled: Email/password sign-in is not enabled for this Firebase project (console → Authentication → Sign-in method).
admin.errRegisterIncomplete: Your login was created, but it could not be listed for review yet. Sign in again later or contact an administrator.
admin.errEmailInUseRegister: This email already has a login — switch to “Sign in”. Your registration is completed automatically on sign-in.
admin.pendingBody: Signed in as {email}. An administrator needs to grant you moderation access before you can review submissions.
admin.bootstrapToggle: Setting up the very first administrator?
admin.claimHint: If this account is one of the project owners listed in the security rules, you can grant yourself access right here.
admin.claimFailed: This account is not on the project-owner list, so it cannot grant itself access. Use the manual steps below, or ask an existing administrator.
admin.bootstrapStep1: Firebase console → Firestore Database → Data (not Authentication — moderation rights are not stored there).
admin.bootstrapStep2: Open the “admins” collection, or start it if it does not exist yet.
admin.bootstrapStep3: Add a document whose Document ID is exactly the account ID above.
admin.bootstrapStep4: Give it a field named “role” of type string with the value “admin”, save, then reload this page.
admin.bootstrapNote: Only needed once. After that, every other account is granted from this page.
admin.registrationsHint: People who registered an account and are waiting for access. Promote the ones you recognize; remove the rest.
admin.moderatorOnly: You are signed in as a moderator. Reviewing submissions happens on the map; only administrators can manage accounts.
admin.createHint: Fallback for when the person can't register themselves. The password is stored only as a hash by Firebase Authentication — share the temporary password securely and ask them to change it via “password reset”.
admin.errEmailInUse: An account with this email already exists.
admin.errInvalidEmail: That email address is not valid.
admin.errWeakPassword: Password is too weak — use at least 6 characters.
admin.errCreate: Could not create the account. Please try again.
admin.revokeConfirm: Remove moderation access for {email}? They will no longer be able to review submissions or sign in as a moderator.
admin.revokeNote: Admins can review submissions and manage accounts; moderators can only review. Revoking removes all moderation rights immediately.
admin.errAction: That action failed. Please try again.

about.heroTitle: How communities reinvent technology to meet their own needs
about.heroIntro: An interactive atlas of real-world examples — from motorcycle taxis in the Philippines to a book written entirely over WhatsApp — of how people creatively adapt mobile and networked technology to the realities of their place and moment.
about.what1: Mobile Networked Creativity (MNC) is not only about the final product or device. It is also about the micro-process of creation — the network of relationships developed among people and technologies in a particular space and time.
about.what2: Across the world, communities — often in resource-constrained or crisis settings — combine everyday objects, mobile devices, and networks to solve problems that formal systems leave unmet. This project collects those stories on a single map so they can be explored, compared, and added to.
about.participate1: Know an example we are missing, or have a photo of one already on the map? Open any case study and use “Add photo or comment” to contribute your own images and reflections.
